title: Multiply/divide by 10, 100, 1000
examples: Teacher, when I multiply by 10, do I move the point?
What do I do if I divide by 1000?
Can you show me where the digits go when I multiply by 100?

explain.say: Today we learn a quick trick for multiplying and dividing by ten, one hundred, and one thousand. We do not move the decimal point at all. Instead, we just move the digits.

items: Move the digits, not the decimal

explain.say: To multiply a number by ten, we simply add one zero to the end of the number. This is like shifting every digit one place to the left. For example, three times ten is thirty. So, three becomes three zero.

Now let us try multiplying a number by one hundred. We add two zeros to the end of the number. This means we shift the digits two places to the left. For instance, five times one hundred is five hundred. So, five becomes five zero zero.
When we divide by ten, we remove one zero from the end of the number. This is like shifting every digit one place to the right. For example, sixty divided by ten is six. So, sixty becomes six.

faq.q: Do I really have to move the digits when I multiply by ten?
faq.a: Yes, you move the digits. Think of it like adding a zero spot for every zero in the power of ten. You can also ask, what is 45 times 10?, or how do I multiply by ten?
asks: How do I multiply by ten?

faq.q: If I divide by one hundred, do I take away two zeros?
faq.a: Yes, you take away two zeros from the end of the number. This is the same as shifting the digits two places to the right. You might also ask, what is 720 divided by 100?, or how do I divide by 100?

faq.q: Does this rule work for numbers with decimals?
faq.a: Yes, it works for decimals too. You still just move the digits and add or remove zeros. For example, two point three times one hundred is two hundred thirty.
asks: Does this work with point numbers?

faq.q: Is it always about adding or removing zeros?
faq.a: It is always about adding or removing zeros based on the power of ten. The number of zeros tells you how many places to shift the digits. You could also ask, what is the pattern here?, or how many zeros do I add?
asks: How many zeros do I add?

faq.q: Can I use a place value chart to help me see the movement?
faq.a: A place value chart is very helpful for seeing the movement. It shows you exactly which column the digits are moving into. You could also ask, can I use a chart?, or show me with a chart.

facts: Multiplying by ten means adding one zero to the right end.
Dividing by one hundred means removing two zeros from the right end.
The number of zeros tells you how many places to shift the digits.
This rule applies to whole numbers and decimals.

quiz.why: You must add two zeros to the end of 45, which gives you 4500.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you move the decimal point instead of adding zeros.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only add one zero, forgetting the hundred part.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you add three zeros, which is too many.

quiz.why: You remove one zero from 780, which leaves you with 78.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you multiply instead of dividing.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you move the decimal point incorrectly.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you do nothing and keep all the digits.

quiz.why: You move the digits three places to the left by adding three zeros to the end of 1.2.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you add too many zeros.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only move the decimal point two places.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only add two zeros.
